question.worked_solution:
Using the linearity property of double integrals, we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}(5{x}^{4}+9{y}^{2})\text{d}A & ={∬}_{R}5{x}^{4}\text{ }\text{d}A+{∬}_{R}9{y}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

The function under the first integral is independent of $y.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}5{x}^{4}\text{ }\text{d}A & =(1-0){\int }_{-1}^{1}5{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{5}{|}_{-1}^{1}) \\  & ={1}^{5}-(-1)^{5} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

The function under the second integral is independent of $x.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}9{y}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A & =(1-(-1)){\int }_{0}^{1}9{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\cdot (3{y}^{3}{|}_{0}^{1}) \\  & =6({1}^{3}-{0}^{3}) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, combining our results, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}(5{x}^{4}+9{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A=2+6=8.\end{aligned}
$$
